Auditor - PwC: Hi Redwood team — for SOC 2 scope please provide a scoped export of keystore access logs and the S3 export/retention policy. Also need repro steps and exact commands to recreate an API 403 the customer saw on 2025-04-21 ~13:12 UTC. Please include timestamps, presigned evidence links, and chain-of-custody manifest.

Priya (security): Acknowledged. We'll need the exact principal/email and a 10-min window to narrow the logs. We'll also collect lifecycle/policy docs and a signed manifest.

Auditor - PwC: principal: svc-api-ingest@customer.com. Window: 2025-04-21 13:10–13:25 UTC. Also saw a billing spike around that time — if related, include meter breakdown.

Ethan (eng): Got it. Quick notes:
- internal log query (example):
  `service:keystore AND request.user:"svc-api-ingest@customer.com" AND timestamp:[2025-04-21T13:10 TO 2025-04-21T13:25]`
- log viewer: https://logs.redwood.internal/explore?q=keystore+svc-api-ingest (internal)
- S3 path for exports: s3://redwood-evidence/soc2/2025/Q2/keystore-access/

Ethan (eng): Repro playbook (minimal):
1) create short-lived service token: `./scripts/mk-token --role keystore:read --ttl 60s --sub svc-api-ingest@customer.com`
2) hit endpoint with an expired token to force 403: `TOKEN=$(cat /tmp/token); sleep 65; curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keystore/access -d '{"key":"probe"}' -v`

Ethan (eng): To export the S3 bucket segment for that day: `aws s3 sync s3://redwood-logs/keystore/2025/04/21/ ./keystore-20250421 --profile redwood-evidence --region us-east-1`

Marta (support): Note on billing: around 13:12 UTC we saw a retry storm from the ingest service — retried 5x per request. Peak RPS during window: ~1,150 (baseline ~140). This likely correlates to auth failures + retries.

Marta (support): Small snippet from our aggregator:
```
{"window_start":"2025-04-21T13:10:00Z","window_end":"2025-04-21T13:20:00Z","peak_rps":1150,"error_5xx":2,"auth_403":47}
```

Sam (infra): Export notes: our S3 lifecycle for evidence buckets is 365 days by policy. The lifecycle rule id is `evidence-retain-365`. Permanent snapshot exports for audits are copied to `s3://redwood-evidence-archive/` and we store md5 manifest and a signed envelope at `/manifests/keystore-2025-04-21.manifest`.

Priya (security): I'll prepare a chain-of-custody manifest (md5, uploader, signed-by) and upload the presigned urls. ETA: will upload artifacts + manifest to the evidence path and ping auditor by EOD 2025-04-25.

Priya (security): Policy link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/security/policies/data-retention (internal) — confirmation: keystore access logs policy = 365 days, audit exports archived 7 years per SOC 2 evidence retention addendum.

Auditor - PwC: Thanks, please include the exact command output for the `aws s3 sync` (or a tarball) and the manifest signed by an oncall/security principal. Also need timeline of who accessed/triggered the retry storm (trace IDs if available).

Ethan (eng): We'll include the `aws s3 sync` output, a tar.gz of the exported logs, and trace IDs. Example trace query for traces UI: `trace.service:keystore AND trace.user:svc-api-ingest@customer.com AND trace.time:[2025-04-21T13:10:00Z TO 2025-04-21T13:25:00Z]`

deploy-bot: Archived logs bundle `keystore-20250421.tar.gz` uploaded to s3://redwood-evidence/keystore-exports/keystore-20250421.tar.gz (presigned: https://s3.redwood.internal/presign/keystore-20250421)

Priya (security): Uploaded manifest: https://s3.redwood.internal/presign/manifests/keystore-2025-04-21.manifest (signed by priya@redwood.com). Also attached `repro-playbook.md` in the bundle with the exact commands above.

Auditor - PwC: Received — will review artifacts and ping if we need deeper sampling. For chain-of-custody please confirm the hash algorithm used (sha256?) and whether any redaction was performed.

Priya (security): Hash: sha256. No redaction performed on keystore access logs; PII removed at ingest so logs are service-principal oriented. If auditor wants a signed statement, we can provide it. :thumbsup:

Auditor - PwC: Perfect. Thanks team, we'll follow up if trace-level detail needed.
